name: Lingaraja Temple
description: One of Bhubaneswar's largest and most visited Shiva temples, the Lingaraja complex is a landmark of Kalinga temple architecture and the centre of the Old Town's temple heritage.
significance: A major living temple and architectural landmark of the Ekamra Kshetra heritage zone.

name: Mukteshwar Temple
description: A compact 10th-century Shiva temple celebrated for its carved torana arch and intricate stone reliefs, often described as a gem of Kalinga architecture.
significance: Important example of early Kalinga temple architecture and its decorative sculpture.

name: Rajarani Temple
description: An 11th-century temple with richly carved exterior walls and a distinctive stepped tower, set in landscaped grounds in Bhubaneswar's Old Town.
significance: Known for its sculptural friezes and unusual architectural details.

name: Parasurameswara Temple
description: A small early temple in Bhubaneswar's Old Town, noted for its carved doorway and historical inscriptions.
significance: One of the older surviving temples in the Ekamra heritage cluster.

name: Brahmeswara Temple
description: An 11th-century Shiva temple with elaborate carvings and a tall spire, located near the Bindusagar tank in Bhubaneswar's Old Town.
significance: Representative of the mature phase of Kalinga temple building.

name: Chausathi Jogini Temple
query: Chausathi Jogini Temple, Hirapur, Khordha, Odisha
description: A small circular open-air temple near Hirapur with niches holding images of the sixty-four Yoginis. It is an ASI-protected monument.
significance: Rare surviving hypaethral Yogini temple associated with Tantric traditions.

name: Ananta Vasudeva Temple
description: A 13th-century Vaishnava temple beside the Bindusagar tank, still active and known for its daily rituals and food offerings.
significance: One of the few major Vaishnava temples in Bhubaneswar's Old Town.

name: Bhaskareswar Temple
description: A small old Shiva temple in Bhubaneswar's Old Town, distinguished by its unusual low, wide form.

name: Jagannath Temple, Puri
description: The principal temple of Lord Jagannath and one of India's major pilgrimage sites, famous for the annual Rath Yatra. The temple complex dates mainly to the 12th century.
significance: A central pilgrimage destination and the focus of Odisha's best-known festival tradition.

name: Gundicha Temple
description: The destination temple of the annual Rath Yatra, located at the end of Puri's Grand Road. The temple is associated with the stay of Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra during the festival.
significance: Closely linked to the Rath Yatra pilgrimage and Puri's ritual calendar.

name: Lokanath Temple
description: A Shiva temple in Puri with a partially buried lingam and a tank beside the shrine, historically linked to the city's older Saiva traditions.

name: Alarnath Temple
description: A Vaishnava temple at Brahmagiri, associated with the period when the Jagannath deities are said to rest during the annual chariot festival.
significance: A pilgrimage stop linked to Puri's Jagannath tradition.

name: Sakhigopal Temple
description: A temple dedicated to Gopala/Krishna at Sakhigopal, an important stop on pilgrimage routes in Puri district.

name: Maa Mangala Temple
description: A Shakti temple at Kakatpur, visited during the Nabakalebara festival cycle when the sacred wood for the Jagannath deities is traditionally sought.
significance: A significant Shakti shrine in coastal Odisha.

name: Ramachandi Temple
description: A coastal temple near Konark dedicated to Goddess Ramachandi, at the junction of the Kushabhadra river and the Bay of Bengal.

name: Tara Tarini Temple
description: A hilltop Shakti temple near Berhampur, reached by steps with views over the Rushikulya river plain. It is a major pilgrimage site in southern Odisha.
significance: One of Odisha's prominent Shakti pilgrimage centres.

name: Samaleswari Temple
description: The principal temple of Sambalpur, dedicated to Goddess Samaleswari and standing beside the Mahanadi river.
significance: The presiding shrine of Sambalpur and a major regional pilgrimage destination.

name: Nrusinghanath Temple
description: A temple at the foot of the Gandhamardan hills, dedicated to Nrusinghanath and known for its stone carvings and hill setting.
significance: An important pilgrimage site in western Odisha.

name: Harishankar Temple
description: A Shiva temple in the Gandhamardan hills near the source of the Harishankar stream, visited for both its shrine and its hill surroundings.

name: Gupteswar Temple
description: A cave shrine dedicated to Shiva in the hills of Koraput district, reached through a forested landscape and widely visited during Shivaratri.
significance: A well-known cave temple and pilgrimage site in southern Odisha.
